situationText: Your teacher asks who wants to answer the first question. You raise your hand and say, "___ want to answer!"

distractors.feedback: Oops! You're the one volunteering to answer. You're not asking your classmate to answer for you!
Nice try, but you're talking about yourself here. That pronoun would make it sound like you're talking about another person!

situationText: Your classmate is sitting beside you during an activity. You ask, "___ have a pencil I can borrow?"

distractors.feedback: Hmm, you're asking your classmate for a pencil. You're not talking about yourself in this question!
Wait! You're talking to one classmate sitting beside you, not the whole class!

situationText: Your brother is chosen as the team captain for your school's basketball game. You tell your friend, "___ is our team captain."

distractors.feedback: Hmm, check the situation again! You're describing the team captain, so bringing the speaker into the sentence changes the meaning.
The team has one captain in this sentence, not a whole group of captains!

situationText: Your sister wins first place in the school's drawing contest. You proudly tell your classmate, "___ won the contest!"

distractors.feedback: Nice try! The sentence is talking about someone else who won the contest, not the person speaking.
Hmm, only one person won the contest here, so check who the sentence is describing!

situationText: You and your seatmate are cleaning your classroom before dismissal. You say, "___ are cleaning our area."

distractors.feedback: Wait! You're cleaning together with your seatmate. You're part of the group, too!
Almost! You aren't cleaning alone—your seatmate is helping you with the area.

situationText: You see three of your classmates practicing for the school program. You tell your teacher, "___ are practicing outside."

distractors.feedback: Hmm, you're watching them practice from the side. You aren't part of their practice group!
Oops! There are three classmates practicing outside, not just one student!

situationText: Your teacher returns your notebook after checking your work. You reach for it and say, "Please give ___ my notebook."

distractors.feedback: Oops! The notebook is being returned to the person who owns it, not to the classmate you're talking to.
Wait! The notebook belongs to one person in this situation, not a group of people.

situationText: You and your friends are waiting for your snacks at the school canteen. You tell the cashier, "Please give the snacks to ___."

distractors.feedback: Oops! The snacks are for your group, not for the person you're talking to.
Hmm, the snacks are for your own group, not for another group of people.

situationText: You see your friends playing basketball at the school court. You tell your classmate, "I saw ___ playing basketball."

distractors.feedback: Hmm, think about your friends as the people you saw in this situation.
Oops! Think about whether you are talking about the people you saw or including yourself in the group.

situationText: [MEMORY]Let's see if you remember. After running during P.E., you tell your friend, "I ____ tired."

distractors.feedback: Almost! Think about the word that fits when you are describing yourself.
Nice try! Remember who is talking in the sentence.

situationText: [MEMORY] After basketball practice, you tell your friend about your brother and say, "He ____ tired."

distractors.feedback: Not quite! You're talking about your brother here, not yourself.
Hmm, you're describing one person after basketball practice, not yourself or a group.

situationText: [MEMORY] Your teacher asks about your group after an activity. You answer, "We ____ ready."

distractors.feedback: Oops! The sentence is about your whole group, not just one person.
Almost! Think about the group being described in the sentence.

situationText: [MEMORY] It's lunchtime, and you tell your friend, "I will ____ my lunch."

distractors.feedback: Not quite! Think about what you're going to do with your lunch.
Oops! You're talking about your lunch, not going somewhere.

situationText: [MEMORY] You just finished playing outside and you're thirsty. You tell your friend, "I am gonna ____ water."

distractors.feedback: Hmm, you're thirsty, so think about what you're going to do with the water.
Oops! You're getting a drink, not heading somewhere.

situationText: [MEMORY] It's recess, and you and your friends are outside the school canteen. You invite them, saying, "Let's ____ to the canteen."

distractors.feedback: Not quite! You're talking about going somewhere during recess.
Hmm, you're heading to the canteen, not asking someone to come toward you.

situationText: [MEMORY] Your friend is waiting for you in the classroom and calls, "Can you ____ here?"

distractors.feedback: Almost! Your friend is asking you to move toward them.
Oops! Your friend is asking you to move closer, not talking about food.

situationText: [MEMORY] You open your pencil case and find only one pencil inside. Complete the sentence: "I have ____ pencil."

distractors.feedback: Hmm, check the situation again. How many pencils are actually inside?
Oops! Count carefully. There aren't that many pencils in the pencil case.

situationText: [MEMORY] You check your school bag and find exactly two notebooks inside. Complete the sentence: "I have ____ notebooks."

distractors.feedback: Not quite! There are more notebooks than that in the situation.
Oops! Count the notebooks again. There are not three.

situationText: [MEMORY] Outside the classroom, you see exactly three students waiting for their teacher. Complete the sentence: "There are ____ students waiting."

distractors.feedback: Hmm, look at the situation again. There are more students than that.
Almost! Count the students one more time. There is one more than two.
